title: A spectral space is a directed inverse limit of finite sober spaces
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space]. Then there are a directed set $I$ (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), finite topological spaces $X_i$ ($i\in I$) which are sober (every irreducible closed subset $Z\subseteq X_i$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] has exactly one point whose closure in $X_i$ is $Z$), continuous maps $f_{ii'}:X_{i'}\to X_i$ for $i\le i'$ with $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ii'}\circ f_{i'i''}=f_{ii''}$ for $i\le i'\le i''$, and continuous maps $p_i:X\to X_i$ with $f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$ for $i\le i'$, such that $(X,(p_i)_i)$ is a limit of the system $(X_i,f_{ii'})$ in the category of topological spaces: the map $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is a bijection of $X$ onto $\{(x_i)\in\prod_iX_i: f_{ii'}(x_{i'})=x_i\text{ for }i\le i'\}$, and the topology of $X$ is the coarsest topology for which all $p_i$ are continuous.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 09XX (label lemma-spectral-inverse-limit-finite-sober-spaces, line 4704), direction 'spectral implies limit', with its proof (via Lemma Tag 09XW (lemma-spectral-closed-in-product-two-point-space), embedding X into a product of two-point Sierpinski spaces, and the images X_J in the finite subproducts; 'detail omitted' twice in Stacks)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the system).* Let $W=\{0,1\}$ with the topology whose opens are $\emptyset$, $\{1\}$, $W$ (so $0$ is a specialization of $1$). Let $\mathcal Q$ be the set of quasi-compact open subsets of $X$, and let $I$ be the set of finite subsets $J\subseteq\mathcal Q$, ordered by inclusion; $I$ is nonempty ($\emptyset\in I$) and directed ($J\cup J'$ is an upper bound of $J,J'$). For $U\in\mathcal Q$ let $\chi_U:X\to W$ be $1$ on $U$ and $0$ on $X\setminus U$; it is continuous, the preimages of $\emptyset,\{1\},W$ being $\emptyset,U,X$. For $J\in I$ give $W^J=\prod_{U\in J}W$ the product topology, let $f_J=(\chi_U)_{U\in J}:X\to W^J$ (continuous, its coordinates being continuous), let $X_J=f_J(X)\subseteq W^J$ with the induced topology and let $p_J:X\to X_J$ be $f_J$ with restricted target (continuous). For $J\subseteq J'$ the coordinate projection $\pi_{JJ'}:W^{J'}\to W^J$ is continuous and $\pi_{JJ'}\circ f_{J'}=f_J$, so $\pi_{JJ'}$ maps $X_{J'}=f_{J'}(X)$ onto $f_J(X)=X_J$; let $f_{JJ'}:X_{J'}\to X_J$ be its restriction (continuous). Then $f_{JJ}=\mathrm{id}$, $f_{JJ'}\circ f_{J'J''}=f_{JJ''}$ for $J\subseteq J'\subseteq J''$ (composites of coordinate projections), and $f_{JJ'}\circ p_{J'}=p_J$.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 09XX (label lemma-spectral-inverse-limit-finite-sober-spaces, line 4704) with Lemma Tag 09XW (label lemma-spectral-closed-in-product-two-point-space, line 4660): the space W, the maps f_U for quasi-compact opens U, the finite subproducts over finite J and the images X_J

proof.text: *Step 2 (each $X_J$ is finite and sober).* $X_J\subseteq W^J$ has at most $2^{|J|}$ points. $W^J$ is $T_0$: if $z\ne z'$ in $W^J$, they differ in some coordinate $U\in J$, say $z_U=1$, $z'_U=0$ (or the reverse), and the open $\{w\in W^J:w_U=1\}=\pi_U^{-1}(\{1\})$ contains $z$ and not $z'$. Hence the subspace $X_J$ is $T_0$ (intersect these opens with $X_J$). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-t0-space-sober] the finite $T_0$ space $X_J$ is sober: every irreducible closed subset of $X_J$ has exactly one point whose closure is that subset.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 09XW (label lemma-spectral-closed-in-product-two-point-space, line 4660): 'If x', x in X are distinct, then since X is sober ... there exists a quasi-compact open U with f_U(x') != f_U(x). Thus f is injective'

proof.text: *Step 4 (every compatible family comes from a point of $X$; first omitted detail).* Let $(y_J)_{J\in I}$ with $y_J\in X_J$ and $f_{JJ'}(y_{J'})=y_J$ for $J\subseteq J'$. For $U\in\mathcal Q$ let $\varepsilon_U\in W$ be the unique coordinate of $y_{\{U\}}\in W^{\{U\}}$. For $J\in I$ and $U\in J$ we have $\{U\}\subseteq J$, and $f_{\{U\}J}$ is the projection to the coordinate $U$, so the $U$-coordinate of $y_J$ is $\varepsilon_U$: $y_J=(\varepsilon_U)_{U\in J}$. Put $C_U=U$ if $\varepsilon_U=1$ and $C_U=X\setminus U$ if $\varepsilon_U=0$. In the constructible topology of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] both $U$ and $X\setminus U$ are subbasic open sets, so $C_U$ is closed and its complement $X\setminus C_U$ (which is $X\setminus U$ or $U$) is open. For every $J\in I$, as $y_J\in X_J=f_J(X)$ there is $x\in X$ with $\chi_U(x)=\varepsilon_U$ for all $U\in J$, i.e. $x\in\bigcap_{U\in J}C_U$. Suppose $\bigcap_{U\in\mathcal Q}C_U=\emptyset$. Then the sets $X\setminus C_U$, $U\in\mathcal Q$, cover $X$ and are open in the constructible topology; this topology is quasi-compact because $X$ is spectral [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-quasi-compact], so finitely many of them, $U\in J$ for some $J\in I$, already cover $X$, i.e. $\bigcap_{U\in J}C_U=\emptyset$, a contradiction. Hence there is $x\in\bigcap_{U\in\mathcal Q}C_U$, i.e. $\chi_U(x)=\varepsilon_U$ for every $U\in\mathcal Q$, and then $p_J(x)=(\varepsilon_U)_{U\in J}=y_J$ for every $J$. (This is the quasi-compactness of $X$ in its constructible topology, on which the closedness of the image of $X$ in the product used by the source rests.)

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 09XX (label lemma-spectral-inverse-limit-finite-sober-spaces, line 4704): 'Then we see that X = lim X_J as sets because X is closed in the product with the constructible topology (detail omitted)'; the closedness comes from Lemma Tag 09XW via Lemma Tag 0A2S (label lemma-fibres-spectral-map-quasi-compact, line 4372), whose proof is the quasi-compactness of the constructible topology, Lemma Tag 0901 (label lemma-constructible-hausdorff-quasi-compact)

proof.text: *Step 5 (the topology; second omitted detail; conclusion).* By Steps 3 and 4 the map $x\mapsto(p_J(x))_J$ is a bijection of $X$ onto $\{(x_J)\in\prod_JX_J:f_{JJ'}(x_{J'})=x_J\text{ for }J\subseteq J'\}$. Let $\mathcal T'$ be the coarsest topology on $X$ for which all $p_J$ are continuous. Each $p_J$ is continuous for the topology of $X$ (Step 1), so $\mathcal T'$ is contained in it. Conversely, for $U\in\mathcal Q$ the set $\{z\in X_{\{U\}}:z_U=1\}$ is open in $X_{\{U\}}$ (the trace of the open $\pi_U^{-1}(\{1\})$ of $W^{\{U\}}$), and its preimage under $p_{\{U\}}$ is $\chi_U^{-1}(\{1\})=U$; so every $U\in\mathcal Q$ is in $\mathcal T'$. Every open subset of $X$ is a union of members of $\mathcal Q$, these forming a basis [def-weil-spectral-space], hence lies in $\mathcal T'$. So the topology of $X$ is $\mathcal T'$. With Steps 1 and 2 ($I$ directed, $X_J$ finite sober, $f_{JJ'}$, $p_J$ continuous and compatible) this is the statement, with $I$ the set of finite subsets of $\mathcal Q$.
